questions.q:
The alkane which is next to methane in homologous series can be prepared from which of the following reactions? I. $\quad 2 \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{Br} \xrightarrow[\text { dry ether }]{\mathrm{Na}}$ II. $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{CaO}, \Delta]{\mathrm{NaOH}}$ III. $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}_2 \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}_2 / \mathrm{Pt}}$ IV. $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{Br} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{H}^{+}]{\mathrm{Zn}}$
Correct answer is
questions.solution:
Homologous series of alkane is $\mathrm{C}_n \mathrm{H}_{2 n+2}$ Methane $\Rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_4$ Ethane $\Rightarrow \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_6$ I. Wurtz reaction
II. Decarboxylation $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{CaO}, \Delta]{\mathrm{NaOH}} \mathrm{CH}_4+\mathrm{CO}_2$ III. $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}_2 \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}_2 / \mathrm{Pt}} \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$ IV. $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{Br} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{H}^{+}]{\mathrm{Zn}} \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_3$ So only I and IV give ethane.

The correct order of rates of addition of Br2/water to the following alkenes is

[A] CH2=CH2

[B] CH2=CH-NO2

[C] CH3-CH2-CH=CH2

[D] CH3-CHCH3|=CH2
options: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="[" close="]"><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></mfenced><mo>></mo><mfenced open="[" close="]"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mfenced><mo>></mo><mfenced open="[" close="]"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mfenced><mo>></mo><mfenced open="[" close="]"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mfenced></math>

questions.solution:
Addition of Br2/ water to the alkene is example of electrophilic addition reaction. This reaction take place in two steps. In first step electrophile is added to the alkene and intermediate carbocation is formed. This step is also called rate determining step. 

So, reactivity of this reaction depends on stability of carbocation formed and as we know for carbocation 3° > 2° >1°. So, reactivity order will be

[B] CH2=CH-NO2 < [A] CH2=CH2 < [C] CH3-CH2-CH=CH2 < [D] CH3-CHCH3|=CH2

questions.q: Benzene reacts with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></math>-propyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>AlCl</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> to give predominantly
questions.solution:
This reaction is known as Friedel Craft's alkylation reaction. in presence of anhydrous AlCl3, n-propyl chloride introduce an alkylating agent. It is an electrophilic substitution reaction. 

Reaction occurs in following step.

Generation of electrophile.

CH3CH2CH2Cl+AlCl3→CH3CH2CH2++AlCl4-

Carbocation formed in step 1 rearranges to form secondary carbocation.

CH3CH2CH2+↔ CH3CH+CH3      1°                    2°

This secondary carbocation attack on benzene ring.

Next step is the abstraction of proton from conjugate base

Hence, the product is isopropyl benzene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following has highest boiling point?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{CCH}_2 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{Cl}$
For isomeric alkyl halides, the boiling points decreases with branching. Branching of the chain makes the molecule more compact and therefore, the surface area decreases. Hence, the intermolecular attractive forces which depend upon the surface area, also become small in magnitude due to branching. Consequently, the boiling points of the branched chain having same molecular formula are less than the straight chain isomers. Higher the molecular weight, higher is the boiling point, but branching reduces boiling point.
